title: ExitReplay: Censoring-Aware Failure Retention for VLA-World-Model Co-Training
hook: VLAW-style loops can add fresh real rollouts yet erase a physical failure from training simply because the new policy no longer reproduces its prefix. ExitReplay adds no real episodes and no accept-or-rollback test: it reallocates the existing replay budget to environment-observed failure traces in proportion to how strongly the current policy is making them disappear.
hook_shape_rationale: This is counter-intuitive minimalism: relative to VLAW-style co-improvement, the real-episode and model-count axes are no larger, because the method uses the same logged episodes and adds only a replay score. A structural-reframe hook was also viable because current-rollout training operationalizes visited-state sufficiency, but it was rejected because the stricter no-extra-real-data comparison makes the testable contribution boundary clearer.

gap_closure.gap: The VLAW and policy-in-the-loop leaves do not determine how much of an observed correction is caused by the environment rather than by the current policy's adaptive censoring of states it no longer visits, so failure evidence can disappear from later cycles without the underlying failure being repaired -- stakes: regressions in avoided or rare contact states can survive until deployment, while repeated-cycle results fail to transfer to policies whose visitation distribution changes differently.
gap_closure.how_closed: C01 relocates the evidence locus from states visited by the current policy to historical, environment-observed failure prefixes and exposes policy-induced disappearance with a checkpoint-relative prefix score; the companion redesigns the fixed replay/start-state generator around that ledger so disappearing failures remain active training evidence. Corpus support is thin in co-adaptive robotics; C01's closest exemplars are empirical security and safety locus shifts, so the claim is scoped to LIBERO and RoboCasa loops rather than broad robot safety.

core_mechanism: ExitReplay moves the co-training evidence locus from the current policy's visited-state stream to a ledger of previously observed failure prefixes. For every failed real LIBERO or RoboCasa trace i, the ledger stores its observations o_{i,0:T}, executed action chunks a_{i,0:T}, native simulator failure label, source policy checkpoint b_i, source world-model checkpoint, and source teacher-forced world-model loss ell_{b_i,i} on the recorded successor frames. Let f_k(o) be the deterministic action chunk emitted by the current open-weight VLA checkpoint and let s be the per-action-dimension interquartile range from the existing benchmark demonstrations; define D_{k,i} as the mean over the prefix of ||(f_k(o_{i,t})-a_{i,t})/s||_2^2, with D_{b_i,i} computed from the stored source checkpoint. The bounded censoring coordinate is c_{k,i}=1-exp(-max(0,D_{k,i}-D_{b_i,i})/tau_c), where tau_c defaults each cycle to the median positive prefix-divergence in the task-balanced ledger and is set to yield c_{k,i}=0 for all entries when no positive divergence exists. Re-evaluating the current action-conditioned video WAM on the same fixed successor frames yields ell_{k,i}; the second coordinate h_{k,i}=ell_{k,i}/(ell_{k,i}+ell_{b_i,i}) (defined as zero when both losses are zero) separates evidence disappearance from improvement on an unchanged physical outcome, and the replay priority is r_{k,i}=c_{k,i}h_{k,i}. The replay sampler uses p_{k,i}=(1-rho)/N+rho*r_{k,i}/sum_j r_{k,j}, falling back to uniform when the sum is zero; rho=0.5 by default and is selected from {0.25,0.5,0.75} using held-out WAM loss on historical failed prefixes. Every sampled prefix is consumed twice: its recorded transitions enter the ordinary teacher-forced WAM loss, and its last pre-failure observation history seeds the baseline World-Gymnast/RISE-style imagined policy rollout so the policy still trains where its own new visitation would have removed evidence. The ledger and sampling weights are stop-gradient bookkeeping computed only from policy forward passes and WAM losses, with no simulator derivative, SVD, sign-mode partition, matched-reset oracle, or sequential candidate-acceptance certificate. The defensible claim is therefore narrow: within existing LIBERO and RoboCasa alternating VLA-WAM loops, checkpoint-relative failure retention can reduce policy-induced evidence attrition under a fixed interaction budget; it is not a general co-adaptation safety guarantee.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 - PREMISES LEDGER
P1. A historical failure prefix becomes less likely to reappear when the current policy's action chunks diverge cumulatively from the actions that generated that prefix; this follows from the sequential dependence of later observations on earlier robot actions, but the adequacy of D_{k,i} as the useful ordering is untested - falsification target.
P2. Teacher-forced WAM loss on fixed environment-recorded successor frames is a comparable within-trace indicator of whether that particular physical transition has become better modeled; it uses the identical pixels and actions across checkpoints and makes no claim that pixel loss is a complete task metric.
P3. Rehearsing a failure prefix in both the real WAM loss and the imagined policy start-state distribution can affect later native task success, rather than only improve bookkeeping loss; untested - falsification target.
OBSERVATION-MODEL. Failure traces are sampled on-policy under historical checkpoints and are therefore selected and incomplete for the current policy; ExitReplay does not treat them as an unbiased sample of all physical states, and estimates only attrition inside the finite accumulated log.
ESTIMAND. At cycle k the diagnostic target is the task-balanced empirical joint distribution of (c_{k,i}, m_{k,i}) over environment-observed failed prefixes in the accumulated log, where m_{k,i}=(ell_{b_i,i}-ell_{k,i})/(ell_{b_i,i}+ell_{k,i}) is the fixed-outcome WAM-repair coordinate, with zero assigned when both losses are zero; no population-level causal effect is claimed.
BLOCK 2 - NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT
The runnable naive version is uniform reservoir replay of all historical failures alongside each cycle's current-policy rollouts. Branch (i): it silently assumes a fixed replay budget keeps rare historical failure prefixes represented as the log grows and the new policy stops resupplying them, which is false by construction; ExitReplay confronts that failure by making checkpoint-relative prefix disappearance, not age, TD error, uncertainty, or current visitation, the replay priority. STANDARD-TOOL FOLLOW-UP: prioritized replay is a textbook tool, so replay itself is not claimed as novel; the domain-specific structure is the full visual-language-action prefix comparison across stored VLA checkpoints and the requirement that one environment-observed trace jointly supplies the WAM real-loss anchor and the imagined policy restart. This is distinct from DAgger's current-policy state aggregation, generic cross-fitting, conservative/short-horizon MBRL, uncertainty filtering, target networks, and ordinary real/imagined mixing, all of which are occupied lineage nodes.
BLOCK 3 - DESIGN RATIONALE
The anchor is kept single-gap because residual-direction alignment and global cycle-sign certification need separate estimands, whereas both ledger coordinates and both training uses share the same historical failure prefix. Density-ratio off-policy evaluation was rejected because high-dimensional action-chunk likelihoods are not reliably available for deterministic or diffusion VLA heads; simulator hypergradients and residual-mode SVD surgery were rejected because the physical simulator is black-box; matched reset-pair or sequential commit tests were rejected because they change the mechanism into an evaluation gate and consume the scarce interaction budget. The chosen forward-pass prefix score is weaker than a visitation-probability estimate but executable for OpenVLA-OFT-style open checkpoints, and its sufficiency is exposed as the falsification target rather than assumed.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Instantiate the existing alternating loop with an OpenVLA-OFT-style open-weight policy, an action-conditioned video WAM in the VLAW or World-Gymnast setup, and the existing LIBERO and RoboCasa simulators; retain each benchmark's native task-success predicate and the baseline's original imagined-rollout horizon.
2. Instrument every real rollout to append each terminal-failure trace, task id, source policy/WAM checkpoint ids, source policy action chunks on its observations, source WAM teacher-forced loss on recorded successor frames, and per-dimension demonstration action scale s to an append-only ledger.
3. At the start of co-training cycle k, run the frozen current policy and each trace's frozen source policy on the stored observations, compute D_{k,i}, D_{b_i,i}, tau_c, and c_{k,i}, and detach these quantities before any optimizer step.
4. Run the current WAM's normal teacher-forced loss on each stored action/successor sequence, compute h_{k,i} and r_{k,i}, and materialize the task-stratified sampling probabilities p_{k,i}; if a task has no failed trace or all priorities are zero, use its ordinary uniform replay branch.
5. Form each WAM minibatch from the baseline current-cycle data plus a rho-controlled ledger sample and apply the unchanged VLAW-style real-transition objective; the sampled old successors are actual simulator observations, not WAM-generated labels.
6. For the policy update, initialize the baseline World-Gymnast/RISE-style action-conditioned video rollout from the stored observation history immediately before each sampled failure, generate alternative action continuations with the current policy, and apply the baseline imagined-advantage objective without adding a new learned judge.
7. Continue all joint updates without accept, reject, rollback, or abstention; after the cycle, append new real failures and recompute the ledger from forward passes, so a policy that routes around an old failure raises its c coordinate instead of deleting the evidence.
8. Log native task success, task-balanced mean c, fixed-prefix WAM loss, and the fraction of sampled prefixes that later reappear under benchmark resets; use these only for the scoped LIBERO/RoboCasa analysis and the registered controls.
falsification_prediction: On the existing LIBERO and RoboCasa simulators, run three matched seeds of an OpenVLA-OFT plus action-conditioned-video-WAM alternating loop with equal real and imagined trajectory budgets for uniform replay, ExitReplay, and a task-and-cycle-stratified score-permutation control. If ExitReplay works, final native simulator task success increases relative to uniform replay while WAM loss on logged failure prefixes that later reappear decreases. The one load-bearing variable is the checkpoint-relative censoring coordinate c_{k,i}; permuting c_{k,i} among failure prefixes within task and cycle while preserving every transition, replay count, rho, and optimizer step should make final native task success return toward the uniform-replay baseline. As an adaptive stress test, add a policy update that deliberately reduces source-prefix action agreement before resuming the same co-training budget; if ExitReplay loses its downstream task-success advantage when this intervention raises c_{k,i}, the relocated-locus mechanism is falsified.
compute_budget: 48 GPU-days on 80GB-class GPUs, at most 8 concurrent, for three seeds of the two benchmarks, registered controls, and the prefix-avoidance stress arm; tight but feasible inside the stated <=50 GPU-day envelope. $0 paid API: policies and WAMs are open-weight and outcomes use native LIBERO/RoboCasa success predicates.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: VLAW refreshes the WAM with the current policy's real rollouts and then improves the policy with synthetic rollouts, whereas ExitReplay constructs a checkpoint-relative prefix-attrition coordinate over historical physical failures and uses it to keep no-longer-visited evidence in both updates.

World-Gymnast optimizes a VLA inside an action-conditioned video model, including an iterative online variant, but does not condition real replay or imagined rollout starts on which environment-observed failure prefixes the changing policy has censored.

RISE separates future prediction from progress-value estimation to produce imagined advantages, while ExitReplay instead preserves historical physical failures through a cross-checkpoint prefix score coupled to WAM loss on the same fixed successor frames.

Feedback World Model corrects future predictions from the current observed next state at inference, whereas ExitReplay retains outcomes from failure prefixes the current policy has stopped reaching and changes the training start-state generator across cycles.

WorldSync aligns predicted intervention effects over broader action coverage, whereas ExitReplay measures cross-checkpoint disappearance of already environment-observed failure prefixes and rehearses them without claiming new action-faithfulness alignment.

what_step_was_missed: VLAW would have needed to retain every failed real trajectory with its source policy checkpoint, recompute current-versus-source action divergence over the full logged prefix, pair that disappearance coordinate with current WAM loss on the same fixed physical successors, and use the joint score to generate both WAM replay and policy imagination starts.
